terra.problem: The passport line jokes about answering the question rather than the Bible story.
“I know why you'd hope so” assumes the baker's feelings.
The text says Manasseh raised altars for Baal, not that he put Baal's name on them.
“He covered the whole place” goes beyond the text, which says he built altars in both courtyards.
“He kept going until both had them” adds a sequence of events the text does not give.
The passage does not say the mediums claimed to reach the spirit world.
Papa Dorin refers to himself in the third person: “Papa will stick.”
Papa Dorin refers to himself in the third person: “Papa has to say no.”
“I get why you'd hope for that” assumes the baker's feelings.
Papa Dorin refers to himself in the third person: “Papa won't dress it up.”
The passage does say more about the garden: Amon is buried there in verse 26.
Papa Dorin refers to himself in the third person: “Papa won't either.”
Papa Dorin refers to himself in the third person: “where Papa leaves him.”
Papa Dorin refers to himself in the third person: “Papa wishes.”
The apple comparison mentions a food other than cookies.
“He didn't start his own thing” claims more than the text says about Amon's actions.
Papa Dorin refers to himself in the third person: “Papa won't make one up.”
“The plot came from his own servants, right there in his home” places the conspiracy in the palace. The text locates the killing there, not the conspiracy.
